key_insight: SeasonStereo makes dense stereo matching work more reliably on satellite images taken at different times, even when seasons, lighting, and appearance change. It uses generative AI to reduce the need for expensive aligned training data and ground-truth geometry.
problem_solved: The paper addresses robust disparity estimation for multi-date satellite imagery, where standard stereo methods struggle because images are not captured simultaneously and their appearance can vary strongly across seasons and illumination conditions.
method: Builds a scalable framework for dense stereo matching across diachronic satellite image pairs.
Leverages generative AI to help handle appearance differences between dates and improve robustness.
Targets disparity estimation without requiring large-scale aligned multi-date datasets with costly ground-truth geometry.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it expands stereo reconstruction to real-world satellite data collected over time, enabling better 3D mapping and monitoring when ideal near-simultaneous image pairs are unavailable. It also reduces dependence on expensive labeled data.

paper_title: SeasonStereo: Robust Dense Stereo Matching for Multi-Date Satellite Imagery via Generative AI
paper_authors: Álvaro Díaz-Laureano, Roger Marí, Elías Masquil, Pablo Arias, Gabriele Facciolo
